sources.title: NPR Topics: Home Page Top Stories

articles.author: Willem Marx
articles.description: The bank is asking a judge to permanently dismiss a lawsuit from Trump-affiliated businesses, arguing a monthslong internal review — not the Jan. 6 riot — explains why hundreds of accounts were shut down in 2021.
articles.title: Capital One says it closed Trump Organization accounts over money-laundering concerns

articles.author: Robbie Griffiths
articles.description: There are at least three fires in and around the city. Large parts of Spokane are under Level 3 evacuation orders, which read: "Leave NOW! This may be your only notice."
articles.title: Thousands of people under evacuation order from wildfires in Spokane, Wash.

articles.author: David Gutman
articles.description: An 18-month investigation by The Seattle Times, KUOW and NPR's Embedded podcast and a review of more than a dozen videos from the night of the shooting reveal the most comprehensive view to date of how the chaotic scene unfolded. And they show how a Black teenager who came to join the civil rights movement of his generation — in a zone abandoned by police — ended up killed by a protest movement that thought he was a threat.
articles.title: A teen was killed at a Seattle protest. New video evidence shows what really happened

articles.author: Diaa Hadid
articles.description: About 1 in 4 babies in the Pakistani fishing settlement of Rehri Goth are born prematurely. Researchers are trying to figure out how to bring the numbers down.
articles.title: Why is the rate of premature births so high in this community?

articles.author: Laila AnnMarie Stevens
articles.description: Laila AnnMarie Stevens documents her family's move from New York City to North Carolina — a kind of reversal of the historic Great Migration of the early 20th century.
articles.title: The Clayton Sisterhood Project: A photographer captures her family's reverse migration from North to South

articles.author: Janet W. Lee
articles.description: NPR asked an aspiring scientist in Philadelphia to interview an adult who is living his dream about his career in conservation science.
articles.title: We asked a first grader to interview his hero: A bird scientist

articles.author: Pien Huang
articles.description: Cyclospora, the parasite that has sickened thousands this summer in the U.S., requires time in the human digestive tract to reproduce.
articles.title: What Cyclospora does inside the gut and how it gets there

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: Police who responded to the shooting found the body of the suspected gunman in an area near the restaurant.
articles.title: Idaho fast food restaurant shooting leaves 3 dead, city spokesman says

articles.author: NPR Staff
articles.description: Trump said Iran and other Middle Eastern countries had asked the U.S. "to hold off any attack" on Iran because "the perimeters of a deal has been agreed to."
articles.title: Trump says he's cancelling Iran strikes, deal pending

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: Vincent Pastore appeared in movies dating back to the 1980s and had roles in big movies including "Goodfellas" and "Awakenings," both in 1990.
articles.title: 'Sopranos' actor Vincent Pastore, known for playing mobsters and tough guys, dead at 80

articles.author: Nick Visser
articles.description:
State corruption watchdog enters second of eight weeks of hearings as part of Operation Rosny. Follow today’s news live
Angus Taylor and Anthony Albanese on leave this week
The opposition leader, Angus Taylor, is on leave for most of this week, his office has announced, with the deputy leader, Jane Hume, acting in his stead.
NSWRL owes a massive debt of gratitude to Laurie for the service he has given to his state as both a player and a coach.
He has also led NSW to arguably two of the greatest Origin series wins of all time as a coach, after ending Queensland’s eight-year winning streak in 2014 and overcoming adversity to steer the Blues home in 2026.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australia news live: Icac hears of alleged Liberal faction push to ‘hit up’ MPs for public money; two hospitalised after Sydney building collapse

articles.author: Benita Kolovos Victorian state correspondent
articles.description:
Former Liberal, ‘anti-woke’ film animator and councillor who says he used to work on Daniel Andrews’ security team among lineup for November’s state poll
One Nation has named its first candidates for the upcoming Victorian state election, as leader Pauline Hanson has vowed to ban the ABC and the Guardian from attending her press conferences during the campaign.
Guardian Australia understands an ABC reporter was refused entry to Hanson’s press conference on Monday, where she announced seven of the eight candidates who will lead One Nation’s upper house tickets. The ABC declined to comment.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: One Nation names eight Victorian election candidates as Hanson bars ABC and Guardian from press conferences

articles.author: Press Association
articles.description:
British band say they are ‘proud to have made this impromptu expression with our fans in Singapore’, where open display of all foreign flags is banned
Massive Attack have called being banned from Singapore a “surreal experience” after displaying a Palestinian flag during their show.
On Wednesday, the English trip-hop collective – whose current lineup includes Robert “3D” Del Naja and Grant “Daddy G” Marshall – played a show at the Star theatre.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Massive Attack speak about ‘surreal experience’ of being banned from Singapore over Palestinian flag

articles.author: Natasha May in Bangkok
articles.description:
Officials are banning some ‘compressed hikes’ which involve walkers tackling demanding routes in short timeframes
Malaysia’s government is tightening hiking rules nationwide after a social media trend left increasing numbers of adventurers needing to be rescued when they became lost or stranded in remote locations.
In the first five months of 2026, Malaysia saw 52 cases of lost hikers, an increase of nearly 30% compared with the same period the previous year, the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department told local media.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Malaysia cracks down on social media hiking trend after jump in numbers needing rescue

articles.author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
articles.description:
Former rugby league player turned TikTok influencer tells parliamentary inquiry his spiralling addiction to gambling cost him about $1m

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Former rugby league star Luke Bateman has alleged gambling company promoters supplied him with cocaine and alcohol, telling a parliamentary inquiry the betting industry exercised no duty of care.
Bateman, who is now a TikTok star and influential in the “BookTok” community, told the inquiry on Monday morning he attended a private Gold Coast event hosted by a gambling company at which senior figures took illicit drugs with clients.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Luke Bateman tells inquiry gambling companies supplied him with cocaine and alcohol

articles.author: Neha Gohil
articles.description:
The new London and South East University Group will be UK’s third largest higher education institution
The UK’s first “super-university”, which will merge the universities of Greenwich and Kent, is set to launch in September.
The new London and South East University Group, to be known as the LASEUG, will have more than 50,000 students on four campuses across London, Medway and Kent, making it the third largest higher education institution in the UK.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK’s first ‘super-university’, merging Greenwich and Kent, to launch in September

articles.author: Agence France-Presse
articles.description:
Authorities issue alert saying indoor spaces without airconditioning are ‘dangerous’ as temperatures pass 40C for fifth straight day 
South Korea has registered its highest temperature since records began more than a century ago, as authorities warned people to “immediately” stop all outdoor activities in affected areas.
The south-eastern city of Yangsan saw the temperature reach 42.5C on Sunday afternoon, the Korea Meteorological Administration (KMA) said, the highest temperature reported since modern weather observation began in 1904.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Stop all outdoor activities’: South Korea records its highest ever temperature

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Wildfires in and around Spokane have stretched ability of federal and local agencies to fight blazes
Wildfires in eastern Washington state forced the evacuation of 60,000 people in the Spokane area while destroying at least 600 homes, businesses and other structures, authorities said on Sunday.
The fires in and around Spokane, the state’s second largest city, burned about 8.2 sq miles (about 21 sq km), but they were among dozens across the western US that stretched the ability of federal, state and local agencies to fight them. A total of about 390 sq miles have burned across the state, and some of the fires, including those in the Spokane area, have not been contained.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Eastern Washington fires destroy 600 structures and force 60,000 to evacuate

articles.author: Sian Cain and agencies
articles.description:
Singer was due to reunite with Wicked co-star Jonathan Bailey in London production of Sunday in the Park With George
Ariana Grande has announced plans to take a break from public-facing work after her tour ends due to “endless, ongoing public scrutiny”. She is pulling out of the upcoming London revival of Sunday in the Park With George.
The pop singer was due to appear opposite her Wicked co-star Jonathan Bailey in a new production of Stephen Sondheim’s critically acclaimed musical at the Barbican in 2027.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ariana Grande to take ‘a step back’ from public life due to ‘endless, ongoing scrutiny’

articles.author: Geneva Abdul
articles.description:
New Order and Simon Armitage among more than 100 signatories to criticise ‘foolish and shortsighted’ cuts
More than 100 artists, writers and scientists have called for the UK government to save the “world’s clearest eyes on the sky”, after funding for thenetwork of radio telescopes at Jodrell Bank Observatory was slashed.
New Order, the Canadian astronaut Chris Hadfield and the poet laureate, Simon Armitage, are among those calling on the new prime minister, Andy Burnham, to save the deep space observatory which includes the Grade I-listed Lovell telescope, prized by astronomers who study galaxies, star formation and planets beyond the solar system.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Artists, writers and scientists urge UK government to save Jodrell Bank Observatory

articles.author: Helena Horton
articles.description:
Decision comes after group of survivors claimed ex-Harrods owner’s associates must have helped facilitate his crimes
At least five victims of the former Harrods owner Mohamed Al Fayed have been confirmed by the Home Office as victims of human trafficking.
A group of survivors of abuse by the deceased businessman had called for the Metropolitan police to make trafficking the main focus of its investigation, arguing that Fayed could not have committed his offences without a steady stream of women sent to him by associates.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: At least five Mohamed Al Fayed abuse survivors confirmed as human-trafficking victims

articles.author: Sarah Butler
articles.description:
Chancellor says the government wants to prevent shoppers being ‘taken for a ride’ at the pump or till 
The chancellor, John Healey, has said the government is standing by to prevent the public from “being taken for a ride at the pump or the till” as the Iran war continues to hit prices.
While he said there had been “no significant evidence of so-called price gouging” during the crisis, he used a weekend column to tell the big retailers that ministers were “watching closely” for any signs of profiteering.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Healey’s profiteering warning on food and fuel risks row with retailers

articles.author: Marina Dunbar
articles.description:
Twin Falls police chief believes Chad Williams, 24, was alone in Saturday attack that killed three people
Authorities say the man accused of opening fire at a fast-food restaurant in Idaho is dead from a self-inflicted gunshot wound, as investigators say quick action by an off-duty law enforcement officer and an armed bystander helped prevent even more bloodshed.
Speaking on Sunday, Matthew Hicks, the Twin Falls police chief, said investigators are confident 24-year-old Chad Williams carried out Saturday’s attack alone.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Suspect in Idaho restaurant shooting died of self-inflicted gunshot wound, police say

articles.author: Ed Pilkington in New York
articles.description:
Health secretary, longtime vaccination skeptic, spent years boosting misinformation about vaccines including MMR
Robert F Kennedy Jr, the US health secretary, on Sunday told American parents that they should get their children vaccinated against measles, as the surge in infections has reached numbers not seen in the past 35 years.
Kennedy, a leading vaccination skeptic who has spent years amplifying misinformation about vaccines, including the shot that protects against measles, mumps and rubella (MMR), made his call in the course of a contentious interview with CNN’s State of the Union on Sunday morning.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: RFK Jr tells US families to vaccinate children against measles amid outbreak

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
Toledo police say Ohio Democrat is active and alert after two-vehicle hit-and-run collision on Sunday
Marcy Kaptur is being treated ⁠for non-life-threatening injuries after a car crash in Toledo, ⁠Ohio, on Sunday, ⁠the ​Democratic US representative’s office said.
Kaptur, 80, was a passenger ⁠in the vehicle and on her way to church, her office ⁠said. Toledo police did not ​respond to ‌a request from Reuters for ‌comment.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US representative Marcy Kaptur taken to hospital after car crash

articles.author: Rory Carroll and agencies
articles.description:
US president claims delay is also in response to requests from Iran and other countries in the region
Donald Trump has said he cancelled planned military strikes against Iran on the basis of “rapidly” reaching a deal on its nuclear programme and the full reopening of the strait of Hormuz.
The US president paused the strikes in expectation of a breakthrough and in response to requests from Iran and other countries in the region, he claimed on his Truth Social platform on Saturday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump backs down on Iran strikes in expectation of ‘rapidly’ reaching a deal

articles.author: Helena Smith in Athens
articles.description:
Greek police say 26-year-old Afghan national is believed to have left Elisabeth-Jane Ross’s body in derelict building 
Greek authorities have arrested an Afghan national in connection with the death of a Scottish woman whose body was found in a suitcase in an abandoned building in central Athens.
Elisabeth-Jane Ross, 38, a charity worker described as an “angel full of innocence and goodness” by friends, had been in Greece for almost three weeks when she is believed to have died.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Man arrested after Scottish woman found dead inside suitcase in Athens

articles.author: Marina Dunbar
articles.description:
Senator Bernie Moreno says congressman and former son-in-law should step down after ex-wife’s allegations
Republican senator Bernie Moreno on Sunday publicly called for Representative Max Miller, his ex son-in-law, to step down from Congress amid allegations of domestic and child abuse.
As recently as Friday, the Ohio senator had avoided giving his opinion directly on accusations made by his daughter, Emily Moreno, against the congressman.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Republican calls for Max Miller to resign from Congress amid abuse allegations

articles.author: Helena Smith in Athens and agencies
articles.description:
Fire department says two-person crew of one aircraft killed in incident during gale-force winds to west of capital
Two firefighting helicopters have collided west of Athens, killing the two-person crew of one of the aircraft, as efforts to control a massive wildfire barrelling towards the outskirts of the Greek capital intensified.
Footage showed one of the helicopters losing control in the face of gale-force winds that have pushed flames towards settlements on Athens’ western fringes.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Two helicopters collide outside Athens as Greece battles to control wildfires

articles.author: Amanda Meade and Jordyn Beazley
articles.description:
The 85-year-old former broadcaster faces 22 charges from six different complainants in what is expected to be a four-month trial

Alan Jones trial live updates

The high-profile trial of former broadcaster Alan Jones for indecent assault and sexual touching charges begins on Monday in Sydney’s Downing Centre local court and is expected to run for four months and hear from 76 witnesses.
Judge Glenn Walsh will hear from six complainants who were allegedly indecently assaulted by the 85-year-old between 2003 and 2020.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Alan Jones trial on indecent assault and sexual touching charges begins in Sydney

articles.author: Jordyn Beazley
articles.description:
Exclusive: Karlene Whitton says her son Matthew Roberts took his own life three months into his jail term. ‘I keep picturing it every night’

Warning: This article contains images and names of Indigenous Australians who have died

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

First Nations advocates warn that prisons in New South Wales could exceed the record number of Indigenous deaths in custody set last year, after two men died this month.
Matthew Roberts, a 27-year-old Bundjalung, Yaegl and Gamilaroi man and father of two young boys, took his life inside Lithgow correctional centre on 7 July after he was remanded in custody in March. Another First Nations man, 21, died a week later at Clarence correctional centre.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: A record number of First Nations people died in NSW prison custody last year. Advocates fear this year will be worse

articles.author: Reuters in Moscow
articles.description:
More than 20 people injured in blast near Italian restaurant Balzi Rossi in centre of Russian capital on Saturday night
A homemade bomb carried by a woman killed three people and injured at least 21 in ⁠an explosion near a restaurant in central Moscow on Saturday evening, prompting speculation on social media that the attack may have been linked to the war in Ukraine.
The explosion occurred just before 8pm local time (6pm UK time) close to an Italian restaurant in one of Moscow’s seven Stalin-era skyscrapers at Kudrinskaya ​Square, police said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Moscow bomb kills at least three as device carried by woman explodes

articles.author: Okba Mohammad and Javier Jennings Mozo in Ceuta
articles.description:
People among the more than 50,000 who entered Spanish enclave this week describe the journey and their prospects
Four days ago, Youssef El Abbas saw an opportunity to reclaim the life he had lost seven years earlier. News was circulating that about 400 people had swum from Morocco to the neighbouring Spanish enclave of Ceuta on the north African coast, approximately 12 miles (19km) across the strait of Gibraltar from mainland Spain.
Here was a chance for the 44-year-old Moroccan father of four to return to Spain, from which he had been deported when his residency expired after the loss of his job in Bilbao in 2019.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Chaos of border crossing gives way to limbo for Moroccans on Ceuta’s streets

articles.author: Lisa O’Carroll Senior correspondent
articles.description:
After years of building lives in UK, potentially thousands of EU citizens could be told they have no right to remain
The UK Home Office has started stripping some EU citizens of their post-Brexit residency rights, in a move that has raised concerns about Britain’s compliance with its withdrawal agreement with Europe.
The UK internal affairs authority has told at least 100 people that they were given residency rights “in error”, disrupting their lives just as they come to the end of their five-year “pre-settled status” and prepare to upgrade to the permanent “settled status”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: EU citizens in UK get letters telling them post-Brexit residency rights were given ‘in error’

articles.author: Jakub Krupa
articles.description:
The measure will impact people travelling by plane or boat between the two countries
Spanish prime minister Pedro Sánchez is now in Ceuta, accompanied by interior minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska.
He first visited the Tarajal border crossing, and is now talking to officials from local authorities, border and police services.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Italy says it’s temporarily suspending EU Schengen arrangement with Spain after 60,000 migrants reach Ceuta – as it happened

articles.author: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg
articles.description:
Activists in the region say politicians regard LGBTQ+ people as ‘the easiest scapegoats to maintain their power’
A growing number of west African countries are implementing or strengthening anti-LGBTQ+ laws, amid local political pressures and a global pushback against LGBTQ+ rights.
In March, Senegal doubled the maximum prison sentence for gay sex to 10 years and criminalised the “promotion” of homosexuality. Niger criminalised “sexual relations with a person of the same sex” in February, the first time same-sex intimacy had been outlawed in the country.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Anti-LGBTQ+ laws are on the rise across west Africa, campaigners warn

articles.author: Dan Collyns in Lima
articles.description:
Aircraft crashes into field after departing from nearby city of Pisco, according to local authorities
Police in Peru report that 13 people, among them foreign tourists, have been killed in a plane crash in southern Peru, near the Nazca Lines.
Local authorities in Nazca confirmed that 11 tourists and two pilots died when the Cessna Grand Caravan crashed in Pueblo Viejo, approximately 4 miles (6km) from the city of Nazca and roughly 12km from the Nazca Lines site.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Tourist plane crashes during flight over Peru’s Nazca Lines, killing 13

articles.author: Lisa O’Carroll in London and Sam Jones in Madrid
articles.description:
Divisions remain in the bloc over mass crossing of migrants into Spanish territory in north Africa
The EU is to hold an urgent meeting of interior ministers on Tuesday amid continued divisions in the bloc over the arrival of more than 50,000 migrants in the Spanish territory of Ceuta in north Africa.
The decision was taken by officials representing EU member states and Frontex border agency experts at what was described as a “sobering” meeting on Saturday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: EU to hold urgent meeting of interior ministers on Tuesday over Ceuta crisis

articles.author: Geneva Abdul
articles.description:
Other members of expedition led by world-renowned climber on Broad Peak also died, climbing company says
A world-renowned Nepali mountaineer and former UK Special Forces member has died after being among 11 climbers caught in a deadly avalanche on Pakistan’s Broad Peak.
Nirmal Purja was killed leading an expedition of 10 other people on the world’s 12th-highest mountain when an avalanche struck at around noon on Thursday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Top mountaineer Nirmal Purja confirmed dead after 11 hit by avalanche in Pakistan

articles.author: Sean Ingle in Glasgow
articles.description:
Tarona Taafaki makes history in women’s 75kg category

All boxers eliminated in semis receive bronze medals

A boxer has made history for ⁠Tuvalu by winning the tiny Pacific island nation’s first Commonwealth ⁠Games medal without winning a single fight.
Twenty-year-old Tarona Taafaki, ⁠one of five entrants in the women’s 75kg category, received a bye to the semi-finals where she lost on an unanimous points decision to India’s Lovlina Borgohain on Friday. At Commonwealth Games, all boxers eliminated in the semis receive bronze medals.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Boxer secures Tuvalu’s first Commonwealth Games medal without winning a bout

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Labour veteran is said to relish role that requires careful negotiation of Trump and impending G20 leadership
Extraordinarily, given the importance of geopolitics, the office of foreign secretary has sometimes appeared a consolation prize in British politics, perhaps reflecting the transfer of responsibility to Downing Street or the Cabinet Office.
That is not how Ed Miliband views the job. His allies say suggestions that he nurses resentment after he was deprived of the chance to be chancellor misunderstand his grasp of the policy challenges ahead. “Ed has an immense appetite to get things done and is relishing being in this job,” one says. “Ed will be a policy-driven foreign secretary.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: EU relations, climate crisis and Gaza: why Ed Miliband is fired up by Foreign Office challenges

articles.author: Agence France-Presse in Singapore
articles.description:
Two members given ‘stern warnings’ after concert and barred from returning, with band also excluded from performing in Singapore again, say authorities
British trip-hop band Massive Attack has been barred from performing in Singapore after an investigation found two members unfurled a Palestinian flag during a concert, police said.
Singapore, known for its tough laws on public speech and assembly, bans the open display of all foreign flags, national emblems or banners without a permit.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Singapore bans Massive Attack for showing Palestinian flag, breaching ban on foreign emblems

articles.author: Robert Mackey and agencies
articles.description:
Treasury secretary’s notepad, photographed by Reuters on Friday morning, prompts questions over US plans
During a cabinet meeting at Camp David on Friday, the US treasury secretary Scott Bessent carelessly revealed plans for the US to buy $5bn-$10bn ⁠in Japanese yen in a scribbled “to do” list left visible to a Reuters photographer.
The image, taken over Bessent’s shoulder during a portion of the meeting open to journalists, showed a Camp David notepad with the underscored words “To Do” followed by “Buy Japanese Yen (JPY) $5-10 bil”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Bessent ‘to-do’ list shows proposal for US to buy $5bn-$10bn of Japanese yen

articles.author: Lucy Campbell (now); Yassin El-Moudden, Tom Ambrose, Taz Ali and Adam Fulton (earlier)
articles.description:
The agreement is a ‘great breakthrough’, the president says in response to media questions

Trump claims agreement for ‘complete disarmament’ of Hamas in Gaza but support uncertain

Saudi Arabia prepares sea and possible land offensive against Houthis

Al Jazeera reporter Hani Mahmoud has reported the mood in Gaza this morning following news of Hamas’s potential disarmament.
Palestinians have heard repeated statements about their fate in the three years since the current war began between Israel and Hamas, so last night’s announcement by Donald Trump wasn’t met with any particular joy or celebration. “There is scepticism and cautiousness among Palestinians,” Mahoud writes from Gaza City in the north of the Strip.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Middle East crisis: Trump says ‘Israel is very happy’ with Gaza peace plan but doesn’t say if withdrawal or Hamas disarmament comes first – as it happened

articles.author: Sam Jones in Madrid, Angela Giuffrida in Rome and Jakub Krupa
articles.description:
Pedro Sánchez decries ‘violation of territorial integrity’ as other EU countries criticise Madrid over incident
At least 57 people have died trying to reach the Spanish enclave of Ceuta after as many as 50,000 migrants entered the tiny territory from Morocco in what Spain’s prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, called “a violation of Spain’s territorial integrity”.
The huge influx, which took place over the course of just 24 hours, overwhelmed the city of 85,000 people, triggered a political crisis for Madrid and led to a mixed reaction from other EU countries, including calls for Spain to be suspended from the Schengen free-movement zone.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: At least 57 people die as tens of thousands cross to Spanish enclave of Ceuta from Morocco

articles.author: Fiona Harvey Environment editor
articles.description:
António Guterres says strengthening El Niño will help push the world’s climate crisis into ‘uncharted territory’
India’s monsoon is in danger and hotter, drier conditions are forecast across much of the world as a stronger El Niño weather system is taking hold, weather experts have warned.
António Guterres, the UN secretary general, said the strengthening El Niño was “adding fuel to a planet already on fire” and pushing the world into “uncharted territory”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: India’s monsoon rains in danger as UN chief warns planet is ‘on fire’

articles.author: Hannah Harris Green in Rio de Janeiro
articles.description:
Injectable PrEP drug holds promise but investment in HIV prevention has declined dramatically worldwide

Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email 

New innovations in HIV prevention could dramatically reduce the number of new HIV cases around the globe, but US foreign aid cuts will mean that those that most need the new medication will be unable to access it, according to experts at the Aids 2026 Conference in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
One year ago, the World Health Organization recommended that governments around the world prioritize expanded access to lenacapavir, an injectable version of the HIV prevention medication PrEP that requires only two injections annually. PrEP, which also comes in the form of daily oral medications and bimonthly injections, is 99% effective in preventing sexually transmitted HIV for people who take it consistently.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: HIV prevention drug could reduce cases globally but USAID cuts prevent access, say experts

articles.author: Presented by Lucy Hough with Julian Borger; produced by Annie La Vespa and Angus Neale; senior producer Ryan Ramgobin
articles.description:
Donald Trump has declared a breakthrough in negotiations over the disarmament of Hamas in Gaza and the withdrawal of Israeli forces, but Israeli government officials have voiced scepticism over the deal.
Lucy Hough speaks to Julian Borger, the Guardian’s senior international correspondent – watch on YouTube
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hamas agrees to Trump’s plan to disarm in Gaza – The Latest

articles.author: Eromo Egbejule in Cape Coast
articles.description:
During visit to Ghana, Sarah Mullally expresses regret and says controversial fund symbolises Christian belief in repentance
At a former British castle where thousands of enslaved Africans were held before being shipped across the Atlantic, the archbishop of Canterbury expressed “lament” for the Church of England’s involvement in transatlantic chattel slavery and reaffirmed her commitment to a controversial £100m fund for affected communities.
Sarah Mullally made the comments during a visit to the Cape Coast castle, a 17th-century fortress built by Swedish traders, but occupied by the Danish and the Dutch, before the British seized it in 1664.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Archbishop of Canterbury vows to support £100m pledge helping communities affected by enslavement

articles.author: Olivia Bowden in Toronto
articles.description:
Data shows Canadians have replaced US vacations with other international trips in apparent rebuke to Trump
Canadians spent $3.3bn less on travel to the US in 2025 than in the previous year, as Donald Trump’s hostile policies towards his northern neighbour continue to incur an economic cost, new government data shows.
The research also indicates that Canadians are not bucking travel overall and instead have replaced US vacations with other international destinations, in a rebuke to Trump’s tariff regime and the president’s continued musings on annexing Canada.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Canadians spent $3.3bn less on travel to US in 2025 after Trump’s return to office

articles.author: Shah Meer Baloch in Islamabad
articles.description:
Local civil rights group alleges authorities removed evidence of killings amid communications blackout
At least 30 people are alleged to have been killed in Pakistan-administered Kashmir in the past two days as part of what has been claimed is a brutal state crackdown that has engulfed the disputed region for weeks.
According to a local civil society group, Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC), the Pakistani security services fired on tens of thousands of peaceful protesters, killing 25 people on Monday and five more on Tuesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pakistan accused of fatally shooting 30 unarmed protesters in Kashmir

articles.author: Oliver Milman
articles.description:
Three years after Maui wildfires many still struggle with ‘biological, emotional and social consequences’, study says
A spate of ferocious wildfires across North America and Europe, worsened by the climate crisis, has incinerated homes and forests and forced thousands of people to flee. Previous fires suggest the effects of these blazes may linger for years to come.
The current fires and their plumes of smoke can appear to be a temporary, if immediate, crisis. Nearly 1,000 fires have sprung into life in the boreal forests of Canada, causing the evacuation of towns and toxic smoke to waft into major Canadian and US cities, prompting threats of retribution from Donald Trump, who bizarrely accused Canada of “poisoning” his country’s air.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Past fires suggest effects of Europe and North America wildfires may linger for years

articles.author: Facundo Iglesia in Buenos Aires and Tiago Rogero in Rio de Janeiro
articles.description:
President also blames Brazil and Mexico and says online critics ‘do not want the ideas of freedom to succeed’
More than a week has passed since Ferran Torres scored the extra-time goal that gave Spain its second World Cup, but – at least for Argentina’s president – the tournament is not over.
Javier Milei has claimed that a coordinated “anti-Argentina campaign” was behind criticism of the country’s team, accusations of racism among its fans and conspiracy theories alleging that Lionel Messi’s side was secretly being favoured by Fifa.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Javier Milei accuses US Democrats of financing ‘anti-Argentina campaign’ at World Cup

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Cockroach Janta party says government has broken promise, with detentions in Delhi, Assam, West Bengal and Bihar
India’s youth-led “Cockroach” movement, whose nationwide protests forced the resignation of the education minister, has accused the government of backtracking on its promise not to act against student protesters and has threatened to restart demonstrations.
The Cockroach Janta party (CJP), which organised mass protests over exam paper leaks and other irregularities, said it had received reports of hundreds of students being detained or “harassed” by police.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: India’s Cockroach movement threatens to restart protests after mass student arrests

articles.author: Natasha May and Jonathan Watts
articles.description:
From Afghanistan to Taiwan, unprecedented deluge highlights devastating impact of climate breakdown
“It rained for 10 days and 10 nights, non-stop – I’d never seen anything like it,” says Anar Gul, a construction worker who lives in the remote district of Dur Baba in eastern Afghanistan.
The houses in his village are built from stone and mud, which makes them extremely vulnerable to heavy rains. After days of rain, Gul’s kitchen collapsed and his neighbour, Sayed Afsar Sadat, saw a large part of his house completely destroyed. “Rains like this are coming heavier and earlier each year,” says Sadat. “They are destroying the roads and washing away our crops. It’s impacting us directly.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘We have lost everything’: extreme rainfall across Asia brings flash floods and typhoons

articles.author: Presented by Annie Kelly, with Oliver Laughland and Calvin Duncan, produced by Rebecca Moore, sound design by Brian McNamara, executive producer Danielle Stephens
articles.description:
Guardian US southern bureau chief Olly Laughland tells the story of Calvin Duncan and a Republican party emboldened in Trump’s America
Calvin Duncan spent 28 years in a notorious Louisiana prison for a murder he didn’t commit. After he was finally exonerated, he decided to run for an administrative role that would allow him to help inmates gain much-needed access to their criminal records.
His journey, from growing up as a Black child in one of New Orleans’ poorest and most violent neighbourhoods to this moment, at 64 years old, pledging to serve the people and ensure others didn’t suffer the same injustices, was extraordinary.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The exonerated prisoner kicked out of office by Republicans – podcast

articles.author: Ed Pilkington in New York
articles.description:
Health secretary, longtime vaccination skeptic, spent years boosting misinformation about vaccines including MMR
Robert F Kennedy Jr, the US health secretary, on Sunday told American parents that they should get their children vaccinated against measles, as the surge in infections has reached numbers not seen in the past 35 years.
Kennedy, a leading vaccination skeptic who has spent years amplifying misinformation about vaccines, including the shot that protects against measles, mumps and rubella (MMR), made his call in the course of a contentious interview with CNN’s State of the Union on Sunday morning.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: RFK Jr tells US families to vaccinate children against measles amid outbreak

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
Toledo police say Ohio Democrat is active and alert after two-vehicle hit-and-run collision on Sunday
Marcy Kaptur is being treated ⁠for non-life-threatening injuries after a car crash in Toledo, ⁠Ohio, on Sunday, ⁠the ​Democratic US representative’s office said.
Kaptur, 80, was a passenger ⁠in the vehicle and on her way to church, her office ⁠said. Toledo police did not ​respond to ‌a request from Reuters for ‌comment.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US representative Marcy Kaptur taken to hospital after car crash

articles.author: Rory Carroll and agencies
articles.description:
US president claims delay is also in response to requests from Iran and other countries in the region
Donald Trump has said he cancelled planned military strikes against Iran on the basis of “rapidly” reaching a deal on its nuclear programme and the full reopening of the strait of Hormuz.
The US president paused the strikes in expectation of a breakthrough and in response to requests from Iran and other countries in the region, he claimed on his Truth Social platform on Saturday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump backs down on Iran strikes in expectation of ‘rapidly’ reaching a deal

articles.author: Marina Dunbar
articles.description:
Senator Bernie Moreno says congressman and former son-in-law should step down after ex-wife’s allegations
Republican senator Bernie Moreno on Sunday publicly called for Representative Max Miller, his ex son-in-law, to step down from Congress amid allegations of domestic and child abuse.
As recently as Friday, the Ohio senator had avoided giving his opinion directly on accusations made by his daughter, Emily Moreno, against the congressman.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Republican calls for Max Miller to resign from Congress amid abuse allegations

articles.author: Shrai Popat in Bangor, Maine
articles.description:
Troy Jackson gained the party nomination for Senate, but now he needs to consolidate support to take on Susan Collins
Troy Jackson is ready to move on.
In fewer than 100 days, the new Democratic nominee has to convince Maine voters to send him to the US Senate – and he’s trying to do it without dwelling on Graham Platner, who dropped out of the race after accusations of rape, which he denies.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Upheaval in Maine and another 100-day campaign - can Democrats pull it off?

articles.author: Nick Robins-Early
articles.description:
New AI models, advanced robots and specialty computer chips are unsettling markets and the US tech industry
Over the past month, a series of advancements in China’s artificial intelligence, chip manufacturing and robotics technologies have rattled financial markets, caused divisions among US tech moguls and left the Trump administration scrambling to respond.
Silicon Valley has long pointed to China’s tech industry as a competitive threat and used its growth as rationale for why US firms should not face regulatory oversight that could slow them down. In recent weeks, however, China’s progress has pushed US tech CEOs past vague warnings and into open disagreement over how to address Chinese-made products upending their industry.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: China’s tech advances are causing chaos from Silicon Valley to the White House

articles.author: Robert Tait in Washington
articles.description:
The US administration has struck a warmer tone of late as Ukraine has shown its value as an ally in the Middle East
As leadership pairings go, Donald Trump and Volodymyr Zelenskyy is not a match made in heaven.
It is a far cry from the warm rapport and kindred spiritedness that defined Ronald Reagan’s relationship with Margaret Thatcher, or even the guarded pragmatic friendliness Reagan forged with Mikhail Gorbachev to effectively end the cold war.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Laura Loomer, Lindsey Graham and the deepening Iran crisis: what’s behind Trump’s reset with Zelenskyy?

articles.author: Timothy Garton Ash
articles.description:
American democrats need a Hungarian-style landslide to overwhelm Trump’s attempts to rig November’s midterm elections
In these days of extreme weather events, it seems odd to say that the US needs a big landslide. But a landslide defeat for President Donald Trump in November’s midterm elections is exactly what is required if the country is to start reversing his deliberate and rapid erosion of its democracy.
The respected Varieties of Democracy (V-Dem) Institute at Gothenburg University argues that in 2025 the US saw one of the most rapid declines in liberal democracy on record. “Democracy in the USA,” says its Democracy Report 2026, “is now at its worst in 60 years.” As the imperial republic marks the 250th anniversary of its founding, the danger seen at the very beginning of its constitutional order by anti-federalists such as Patrick Henry – that of an overmighty president abusing his executive power in an attempt to become a new king – has come closer than ever before.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The Democrats have one last chance to halt the erosion of US democracy – and it’s less than 100 days away | Timothy Garton Ash

articles.author: Hosted by Carter Sherman , produced by Meg Driscoll, engineered by Ivan Kuraev , executive producer Jonathan Menjivar
articles.description:
With Republicans' chances in the midterms looking shaky, Donald Trump is increasingly trying to rewrite the rules that govern US elections. Voting rights groups say he's really laying the groundwork to suppress voters. Trump has already moved to change mail-in voting, but he now wants Congress to pass the Save America Act, which includes strict voter ID restrictions. He's also accused China of interfering in the 2020 election. (Trump didn't back up that claim with evidence.) Host Kai Wright speaks with Garrett Epps, legal affairs editor at Washington Monthly, about the threat to US elections and what voters can do to protect them.

Read Garrett Epps' story in Washington Monthly

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Will the US midterm elections be free and fair? – Stateside with Kai and Carter

articles.author: Presented by Lucy Hough with Julian Borger ; produced by Annie La Vespa and Angus Neale ; senior producer Ryan Ramgobin
articles.description:
Donald Trump has declared a breakthrough in negotiations over the disarmament of Hamas in Gaza and the withdrawal of Israeli forces, but IsraelI government officials have voiced scepticism over the deal.

Lucy Hough speaks to Julian Borger, the Guardian’s senior international correspondent
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Can Trump’s Hamas disarmament plan work and will Israel agree to withdraw from Gaza? - The Latest

articles.author: Judith Levine
articles.description:
Trump’s campaign of repression echoes the red scare. But now the government has bigger ambitions and more powerful tools
There are many parallels between the first McCarthy era, roughly 1946 to 1956, and Trump’s campaign of political repression, his own updated McCarthyism.
Both regimes crafted a monster of quasi-facts and innuendo and fed it with fear: an enemy within, well-organized and financed, secretive and violent, allied with evil foreigners and bent on overthrowing capitalism, democracy and Christian morality. Both used flagrantly unconstitutional means to cleanse the nation of the spectral menace.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: McCarthyism has returned to the United States – and this time it’s even more dangerous | Judith Levine

articles.author: Margaret Sullivan
articles.description:
The conservative columnist Ross Douthat is the network’s latest perplexing hire – but the move is in line with the new leadership
In media circles, this week’s hire of a prominent New York Times columnist as a correspondent for CBS’s 60 Minutes was greeted with disbelief.
The collective response went something like this: “What?!”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: No TV experience? At CBS News, that’s no problem | Margaret Sullivan

articles.author: Sunny Patel
articles.description:
Francesca Hong, a candidate for Wisconsin governor, is part of a wave of democratic socialists finding traction with an old idea
In a matter of weeks, Francesca Hong, an unlikely candidate for governor in one of the country’s most heated battleground states, will test a message that is at once radical and, to many, incredibly practical: the government should help pay for childcare.
“When we talk about free childcare, you can connect to folks whether it’s on an economic argument or just purely that it’s the right thing to do for our kids,” said Hong, a democratic socialist running in Wisconsin’s Democratic primary on 11 August. “I always like to remind folks: if we don’t take care of our kids, who’s going to take care of us?”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How free childcare started winning US elections: ‘Overnight, people realized how essential it was’

articles.author: Matt Gurney
articles.description:
The White House fails to understand that Mark Carney and Canada’s regional leaders can’t cave in to the US president: it’s too toxic to voters
• Matt Gurney is a journalist based in Toronto
Though many hate to admit it, Canadians have long wished for more attention from the US. Well, we’re getting it now. And it turns out that President Trump and some of his top supporters in the Maga movement don’t much like us.
The first big hint was when he started talking about annexing us, saying we couldn’t survive without American support. But the most recent example of Trump’s dislike for Canada can be seen in his latest tariff policies. Canada was largely spared the impact of his “Liberation Day” tariffs in April 2025 by its pre-existing free trade deal with the US (and Mexico), but earlier this month, as expected, the US declined to extend that deal for another 16-year term. It’s now subject to annual renegotiations. Then, last week, the White House announced tariffs as high as 50% on a selection of Canadian products including, for the first time, items previously protected by the trade agreement. The US called it retaliation for Canadian trade practices.
Matt Gurney is a journalist based in Toronto, and co-editor of The Line, an online magazine
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump has singled out us Canadians for special treatment in his tariff war – there is no choice but to get nasty | Matt Gurney

articles.author: Hosted by Kai Wright and Carter Sherman , with David Smith and Rachel Leingang . Produced by Suzanne Gaber and Tiara Chiaramonte , edited by Anabel Bacon , engineered by Ivan Kuraev
articles.description:
Earlier this year, Congress reached a depressing milestone: 86% of Americans, a record high, disapproved of its job performance. But this summer, there have been some signs that shifts are underway. On the left, House Democrats have just voted in unprecedented numbers to withhold military aid from Israel, and across the country, progressive candidates are running competitive primary campaigns that are energizing a base fed up with the status quo. On the right, Republicans are reeling from the sudden death of Lindsey Graham, the South Carolina senator and one of Donald Trump's staunchest supporters. Mitch McConnell, the former Senate majority leader, remains sequestered following a health scare in June, raising questions of if a changing of the guard might be underway there, too. Kai Wright and Carter Sherman are joined by David Smith, the Guardian's Washington bureau chief and Rachel Leingang, midwest political correspondent, to discuss gerontocracy, transparency, the rise of the Democratic Socialists of America and just how much of an inflection point this summer might be for both parties


This page was amended on 23 July 2026. A previous version misspelled Lindsey Graham. 

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Is US Congress finally on the verge of a change? – Stateside with Kai and Carter

articles.author: Sam Levine Zhara Keogh Michael Kalenderian Sarah Bertram
articles.description:
Donald Trump delivered a primetime address to the country on Thursday, claiming that declassified intelligence showed Chinese interference in US elections. The US president revived long-running attacks on election security, despite a US intelligence assessment that found no evidence Beijing altered the 2020 vote, which he lost. The Guardian's voting rights reporter Sam Levine factchecks some of Trump's claims

Trump is invoking foreign election interference to justify his own - Opinion

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Fact-checking Donald Trump’s address on Chinese election interference – video

articles.author: Neha Gohil
articles.description:
The new London and South East University Group will be UK’s third largest higher education institution
The UK’s first “super-university”, which will merge the universities of Greenwich and Kent, is set to launch in September.
The new London and South East University Group, to be known as the LASEUG, will have more than 50,000 students on four campuses across London, Medway and Kent, making it the third largest higher education institution in the UK.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK’s first ‘super-university’, merging Greenwich and Kent, to launch in September

articles.author: Sian Cain and agencies
articles.description:
Singer was due to reunite with Wicked co-star Jonathan Bailey in London production of Sunday in the Park With George
Ariana Grande has announced plans to take a break from public-facing work after her tour ends due to “endless, ongoing public scrutiny”. She is pulling out of the upcoming London revival of Sunday in the Park With George.
The pop singer was due to appear opposite her Wicked co-star Jonathan Bailey in a new production of Stephen Sondheim’s critically acclaimed musical at the Barbican in 2027.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ariana Grande to take ‘a step back’ from public life due to ‘endless, ongoing scrutiny’

articles.author: Geneva Abdul
articles.description:
New Order and Simon Armitage among more than 100 signatories to criticise ‘foolish and shortsighted’ cuts
More than 100 artists, writers and scientists have called for the UK government to save the “world’s clearest eyes on the sky”, after funding for thenetwork of radio telescopes at Jodrell Bank Observatory was slashed.
New Order, the Canadian astronaut Chris Hadfield and the poet laureate, Simon Armitage, are among those calling on the new prime minister, Andy Burnham, to save the deep space observatory which includes the Grade I-listed Lovell telescope, prized by astronomers who study galaxies, star formation and planets beyond the solar system.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Artists, writers and scientists urge UK government to save Jodrell Bank Observatory

articles.author: Helena Horton
articles.description:
Decision comes after group of survivors claimed ex-Harrods owner’s associates must have helped facilitate his crimes
At least five victims of the former Harrods owner Mohamed Al Fayed have been confirmed by the Home Office as victims of human trafficking.
A group of survivors of abuse by the deceased businessman had called for the Metropolitan police to make trafficking the main focus of its investigation, arguing that Fayed could not have committed his offences without a steady stream of women sent to him by associates.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: At least five Mohamed Al Fayed abuse survivors confirmed as human-trafficking victims

articles.author: Sarah Butler
articles.description:
Chancellor says the government wants to prevent shoppers being ‘taken for a ride’ at the pump or till 
The chancellor, John Healey, has said the government is standing by to prevent the public from “being taken for a ride at the pump or the till” as the Iran war continues to hit prices.
While he said there had been “no significant evidence of so-called price gouging” during the crisis, he used a weekend column to tell the big retailers that ministers were “watching closely” for any signs of profiteering.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Healey’s profiteering warning on food and fuel risks row with retailers

articles.author: Morgan Ofori
articles.description:
Lowe says the two should put ‘personalities and our past disagreements aside for good of the country’
The leader of Restore Britain, Rupert Lowe, has extended an olive branch to Nigel Farage, saying the two should put “personalities and our past disagreements aside for the good of the country”.
Lowe told the Reform UK leader that if he was “prepared to work together around serious policies, serious reform and serious government, then so are we”.
Mass deportation of illegal migrants “including women and children”.
Tougher rules on legal migration, a ban on halal and kosher slaughter, the burqa, cousin marriage and sharia courts.
A referendum on the death penalty.
Welfare cuts to fund “self-sufficiency”.
The exclusion of former Tory ministers from any future cabinet.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rupert Lowe urges Nigel Farage to work with Restore Britain

articles.author: Helena Smith in Athens
articles.description:
Greek police say 26-year-old Afghan national is believed to have left Elisabeth-Jane Ross’s body in derelict building 
Greek authorities have arrested an Afghan national in connection with the death of a Scottish woman whose body was found in a suitcase in an abandoned building in central Athens.
Elisabeth-Jane Ross, 38, a charity worker described as an “angel full of innocence and goodness” by friends, had been in Greece for almost three weeks when she is believed to have died.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Man arrested after Scottish woman found dead inside suitcase in Athens

articles.description:
Speaking in Dover, the prime minister pledged to be committed to tackling the issue but also said safe routes for refugees were necessary to 'take away the selling point' of trafficking gangs
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Andy Burnham promises to be relentless in tackling small boat crossings – video

articles.author: Alexandra Topping Political correspondent
articles.description:
Prime minister says UK needs to ‘bring back that control’ and safe routes for refugees are necessary to tackle trafficking
Andy Burnham has pledged to be “relentless” in tackling small boat crossings after tens of thousands of migrants entered the Spanish territory of Ceuta, and he said “safe routes” for refugees were necessary to tackle trafficking gangs.
Speaking during a visit to Dover, the prime minister said he had been assured by the Spanish prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, that approximately 98% of the estimated 50,000 people who entered Spain’s north African territory of Ceuta last week had now been returned to Morocco.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burnham to be ‘relentless’ on small boat crossings after Ceuta crisis

articles.author: Helena Horton
articles.description:
Farmers battle to salvage what they can of their crops as heatwave set to continue
Britain could face shortages of certain foods after punishing drought in parts of England, the National Farmers’ Union (NFU) has warned as a heatwave was forecast to continue into next week.
The UK’s Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has issued heat health alerts for eight regions of England, with temperatures set to rise above 30C in parts of the country. UKHSA said rising temperatures may increase health risks, particularly for vulnerable groups.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Britain could face food shortages as drought continues, farmers warn

articles.author: Neha Gohil and PA Media
articles.description:
Harrison Simpson was subject of arrest warrant for breach of court order 18 months before killing girlfriend’s daughter
Cleveland police failed to arrest a paedophile for breaching a non-molestation order, 18 months before he sexually assaulted and murdered and his girlfriend’s two-year-old daughter, a court heard.
Isabelle Welsh died on 14 September 2025 after what police described as a “campaign of violence” against her. The two-year-old collapsed at her home in Teesside after weeks of abuse that left her covered in bruises and with 21 broken bones.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Cleveland police failed to arrest man who later killed two-year-old girl

articles.author: Dalya Alberge
articles.description:
Exclusive: Outsourced guards, largely from minority ethnic backgrounds, barred from staff hub for mainly white employees
The National Gallery’s security staff, of whom the vast majority are from minority ethnic backgrounds, are facing shocking segregation, a senior curator has claimed.
Its outsourced guards are barred from the building’s high-quality “hub” – bright and airy recreation rooms that are available to the institution’s mainly white employees. They are not allowed to take their breaks there, or even sit in that area.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: National Gallery security staff segregated like ‘second-class citizens’, curator claims

articles.author: Alexandra Topping Political correspondent
articles.description:
Labour chair accuses Reform of making ‘grubby pacts’ after contradictory reports emerge on timeline of events
Reform UK is operating under a “stench of sleaze”, Labour has said, after reports that Nigel Farage struck a secret deal to return as leader of Reform months before the general election.
Farage was in discussions about a return to the political frontline from as early as March 2024, despite later claiming he had no intention of returning to politics until June 2024, the Sunday Times reported.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Stench of sleaze’: Farage struck deal over political return months before 2024 election, reports say

articles.author: Pippa Crerar, political editor
articles.description:
New education secretary says it is ‘false trade-off’ by critics to suggest schools cannot pursue academic excellence alongside technical skills
Lucy Powell has said she wants to be an ambitious “tiger mum” for all young people, whatever their route through education, after the government was accused of dumbing down England’s schools with plans to create more vocational routes.
The new education secretary said secondary pupils should be able to pursue academic excellence as well as high-quality vocational training, and it was a “false trade-off” to suggest schools could not provide both.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Tiger mum’ Lucy Powell on Labour’s vocational skills drive: ‘It’s about ambition for everybody’

articles.author: Mark Brown North of England correspondent
articles.description:
Volunteers painstakingly gather plastic pellets washing up on beaches after ship collision on 19 July
‘You’ve got a local community that really cares about the coastline,” said Alice Laverty, reflecting on the huge army of volunteers who had taken to crisis-hit beaches in north-east England with passion and only the most basic tools. “They’ve all got a dustpan, a brush, a bucket, a kitchen sieve.”
On beaches from Cambois in Northumberland to Seaburn on Wearside, up to 2,000 dedicated volunteers have been painstakingly sifting through sand to find tiny, lentil-sized pellets of plastic.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘There’s no nurdle fairy’: thousands mobilise to clean up plastic spillage in north-east England

articles.author: Lisa O’Carroll Senior correspondent
articles.description:
After years of building lives in UK, potentially thousands of EU citizens could be told they have no right to remain
The UK Home Office has started stripping some EU citizens of their post-Brexit residency rights, in a move that has raised concerns about Britain’s compliance with its withdrawal agreement with Europe.
The UK internal affairs authority has told at least 100 people that they were given residency rights “in error”, disrupting their lives just as they come to the end of their five-year “pre-settled status” and prepare to upgrade to the permanent “settled status”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: EU citizens in UK get letters telling them post-Brexit residency rights were given ‘in error’

articles.author: Sarah Butler
articles.description:
As boss Stuart Machin unveils a new-look Pantheon the retailer has fashion and overseas challenges ahead
On a hot summer’s evening on London’s busy Oxford Street, a crowd of fashion influencers, models, journalists and the odd City analyst gathered for a first look at the upmarket revamp of Marks & Spencer’s landmark Pantheon store.
Some may have had to double-check they had the right address, such is the scale of the makeover at the 88-year-old outlet, which is intended as a blueprint for change across the retailer’s more than 200 large stores.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Inside M&S’s swanky Oxford Street revamp, the blueprint for its £700m growth strategy

articles.author: Bethan McKernan
articles.description:
Visible impact of warming climate is impossible to ignore across landscapes that have been starved of rainfall
Half of England and the whole of Wales are officially in drought and July is set to be the driest month on record as extreme heat intensified by the climate crisis continues to grip the UK and Europe this summer.
The announcements this week by England’s Environment Agency and Natural Resources Wales mark the third such event over the past five years, and come in the wake of four record-breaking heatwaves since May which have fuelled huge wildfires and left farmers, wildlife and protected habitats running out of water.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Relentless UK heatwaves turn ‘green and pleasant land’ brown

articles.author: Aisha Down, Dan Milmo and Graeme Wearden
articles.description:
Investors scramble to make sense of a shock Chinese challenge to the dominance of western chipmakers
Even for the rollercoaster world of AI, last week was particularly volatile as investors scrambled to keep up with developments that threatened the dominance of the largest western chipmakers.
It began with a double whammy. On Monday, the Chinese memory chipmaker CXMT floated on the Shanghai stock market, soaring by 466% in value to 3.3tn yuan (£365bn).
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Stock market turmoil sheds stark light on the opaque AI economy

articles.author: Sandra Laville Environment correspondent
articles.description:
Council leaders say crumbling infrastructure and lack of water are jeopardising government’s plans for new homes
The government’s housebuilding agenda is hitting the stark reality of a lack of water and crumbling infrastructure across the east and south-east of England.
Half the country was declared to be in serious drought this week, for the second consecutive year, with the Environment Agency warning of dire consequences for the economy, environment and wildlife.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘We cannot magic up more water’: the supply problems putting housing targets in England at risk

articles.author: Rob Davies
articles.description:
Exclusive: French company Puy du Fou worked with a sanctioned oligarch on plans for a Crimea resort longer than disclosed, and later courted Iran and China
In February 2014, thousands of “little green men” – Russian soldiers in unmarked uniforms – flooded into Crimea, seizing control of military bases and infrastructure.
Their arrival marked the opening salvo of Vladimir Putin’s annexation of the peninsula, an operation that ultimately escalated into the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Kremlin connections: the Russia links to a £600m UK theme park

articles.author: Kalyeena Makortoff Banking correspondent
articles.description:
Security lapse leaves sensitive information and contact details of 51 government officials exposed for 40 hours
The public body in charge of the UK’s state investments has been pushed to improve its internal security after a data breach left “high-level management information” publicly accessible for nearly two days.
UK Government Investments (UKGI), the agency that manages the taxpayers’ interest in a swathe of companies including Channel 4 and the Post Office, said the security failure also left more than 50 government officials’ personal details exposed for nearly 40 hours.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK’s state investments agency hit by data breach

articles.author: Josh Halliday and Aletha Adu
articles.description:
PM argues for codified model of decentralisation that would fundamentally change centuries-old workings of state
Andy Burnham has said his programme of devolution strengthens the case for a written constitution for the UK, a move that would fundamentally alter the workings of the state that have developed over centuries.
The prime minister has long believed the UK’s “antiquated” political system needs a dramatic overhaul if opportunity is to be shared equally across the country.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Devolution plans strengthen case for written UK constitution, says Burnham

articles.author: Helena Horton
articles.description:
Britons move away from trend of grey paving and pristine lawns in an embrace of colour, with lavender a top choice
If you manage to spot a garden in bloom this summer, beyond the strips of bleached and torched grass, there may be one colour you see more than any other: purple, the horticultural hue of the season.
Plants such as lavender, salvias and catmint are in vogue, according to the Royal Horticultural Society (RHS), which conducted extensive research into the colours Britons best love to see in their gardens.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Purple reign: how shade became British gardeners’ favourite

articles.author: Kevin Rawlinson
articles.description:
Some in Dover say their town is being exploited by content creators and politicians, but others claim there is a genuine problem
If you believe rightwing influencers and politicians, Dover and the wider Kent coast has been the site of an “invasion” for years now. And, for an online audience of millions, they and their camera crews have been the vanguard in the nation’s defence.
Indeed, if you believe all you see on the algorithms of amateur Channel watchers, the shadow home secretary, Chris Philp, braved a hail of French gunfire as he took to the water in a fishing boat this week; an attempt by the French authorities, he suggested, to deter him in his mission of highlighting the small boats crisis.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: On the ground in the English seaside town rightwing influencers say is being ‘invaded’

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Labour veteran is said to relish role that requires careful negotiation of Trump and impending G20 leadership
Extraordinarily, given the importance of geopolitics, the office of foreign secretary has sometimes appeared a consolation prize in British politics, perhaps reflecting the transfer of responsibility to Downing Street or the Cabinet Office.
That is not how Ed Miliband views the job. His allies say suggestions that he nurses resentment after he was deprived of the chance to be chancellor misunderstand his grasp of the policy challenges ahead. “Ed has an immense appetite to get things done and is relishing being in this job,” one says. “Ed will be a policy-driven foreign secretary.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: EU relations, climate crisis and Gaza: why Ed Miliband is fired up by Foreign Office challenges

articles.author: Anna Isaac
articles.description:
Nigel Farage’s £5m gift, the Cottrell family’s links and donations, and Richard Tice’s business dealings form part of an increasingly clear nexus of relationships
It has been three months since the Guardian revealed that Nigel Farage had accepted a £5m gift from Christopher Harborne, a billionaire donor to Reform UK.
This was not the first story in our continuing investigation. But it has proved the most significant, and the consequences of the disclosure are still being played out.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The tangled financial web at the heart of Reform UK

articles.author: Ben Beaumont-Thomas
articles.description:
Duetting stars surpass record set in 1953, when crooner Frankie Laine hit the top with I Believe
Sam Fender and Olivia Dean have scored the longest running UK No 1 single in history with Rein Me In, beating a record that has stood since 1953.
Back then, the UK singles chart had been running for less than a year and contained just 12 songs when I Believe, a bombastic ballad by US crooner Frankie Laine, hit No 1 and spent a total of 18 weeks on the chart.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Sam Fender and Olivia Dean’s Rein Me In breaks 73-year record to become longest-running UK No 1 single

articles.description:
A Guardian investigation has revealed that a political lobbying firm, founded by the former electoral strategist for David Cameron and Boris Johnson, secretly pays journalists to write pieces for British newspapers that are favourable to its clients.

In a statement, CT Group said: 'We do not comment publicly on work we do for clients and we therefore cannot respond to the specific allegations you have made.' CT Group said the events had been 'deliberately mischaracterised' and it did not engage the undercover journalist to do anything and did not pay him anything. It said the journalist was looking for work and 'chased us relentlessly over a period of more than six months'

Boom in solar farms and home installations in first half of 2026 began shortly after start of US-Israel war against Iran
Great Britain has recorded more new solar power installations in the first half of this year than in any six-month period since 2011, as households turn to rooftop panels to help cut their energy bills.

articles.author: Geneva Abdul and Peter Walker
articles.description:
Several councils to stop housing tenants in glass-fronted Britannia Point in London, where tenants were earlier told they could not use air con
As the fourth heatwave of the year hit the UK on Wednesday, Benice Bodah and her three teenage sons braced for more scorching temperatures inside their south-west London home. The two-bedroom flat has a built-in air-conditioning unit, but it has worked only intermittently in the almost three years since the family were placed in temporary accommodation at Britannia Point in Colliers Wood. “It has not been easy, but what can we do?” said Bodah, 48.
Several councils have now agreed to stop housing families in emergency accommodation in the glass-fronted block after the Guardian revealed they had been told they couldn’t use the air-conditioning during heatwaves as it had “not been offered as an amenity” for them. The 19-storey building is owned by Criterion Capital, set up by the billionaire property magnate Asif Aziz. The temporary tenancies can last from weeks to years and are managed separately by letting agencies, including the London-based Aura Assets Management.

articles.description:
UKHSA estimates 2,877 fatalities during heatwaves in May and June, almost twice that recorded in 2025 season
England is on track to record its highest ever number of heat-related deaths this summer after the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) announced that an estimated 2,877 people had died in the May and June heatwaves.
The record was set in 2022 with 2,985 deaths, and August, traditionally the hottest month, is yet to arrive. The health secretary, Yvette Cooper, said: “My thoughts are with all those who have lost loved ones as a result of the long and intense heatwaves.”

Introducing the legislation would be ‘very challenging’ until care system improved, PM says

Andy Burnham has said the assisted dying debate needs to wait until palliative care and social care are fixed, as he set out his path to resolving one of the most intractable problems in British politics.

articles.description:
As Pokémon Go celebrates its 10th anniversary, its devoted players explain how the game has created a vibrant intergenerational community spanning the globe
Most Pokémon obsessives count rare, absurdly expensive playing cards or pristine, fully boxed game cartridges that have survived decades in the attic among their most prized possessions. But for Mairead Ralph, her Pokémon-related crown jewel is a bit different. “Technically, it’s my husband!” she says.
The pair first locked eyes amid decks of Pokémon playing cards and Pokéballs at a fan event 16 years ago and the rest is history. Ralph was among hundreds of Pokémon fans who flocked to Shoreditch, east London, on Saturday afternoon for a pop-up celebrating the 10th anniversary of Pokémon Go, the massively successful augmented reality smartphone game that has seen millions of players physically venture to all corners of the earth to catch ’em all in person. In that spirit, the surrounding area was full of Pokéheads wandering the streets, their heads in their phones, seeking to catch exclusive Pokémon that had been released.

Over the past month, a series of advancements in China’s artificial intelligence, chip manufacturing and robotics technologies have rattled financial markets, caused divisions among US tech moguls and left the Trump administration scrambling to respond.
Silicon Valley has long pointed to China’s tech industry as a competitive threat and used its growth as rationale for why US firms should not face regulatory oversight that could slow them down. articles.author: Isabelle Aron
articles.description:
Sick of doomscrolling? From venues with smartphone swear jars to cabins with absolutely no signal, here are the fun and freeing ways to ditch your device
There’s a ritual at the start of every event hosted by the Offline Project. Run by Pelé Zachariah, the activities vary – it could be a group walk, a collage‑making class or a supper club – but each one begins in the same way, *with an invitation to hand over your phone. Devices go in a lockbox. Once they’re all in, Zachariah closes the door and turns the key. “I don’t place them in for people, because it’s nice for them to physically put it in the box themselves, walk away, and think: for the next two or three hours, I’m fully present.”
He has been running these screen-free events in London since August 2025. First-timers can be apprehensive about being separated from their phone. “You can sense the vibe when they’re putting it away,” says Zachariah. “People have said to me, ‘I felt really weird’ or ‘I felt super uncomfortable for the first few minutes not having my phone on me.’ Then they’ll say, ‘I didn’t know how much I needed that.’”

articles.author: Jasper Jolly
articles.description:
Live, rolling coverage as London’s biggest companies defy Middle East disruption and UK petrol prices rise to around £1.60 per litre, the highest since Donald Trump ordered renewed strikes
The story piquing the interest of the financial press this morning is that of Leopold Aschenbrenner, the AI Wunderkind (he’s German-born) who has been forced to sell off his fund in a fire sale after the AI boom ran out of steam.
The 24-year-old had persuaded a lot of people to give him a lot of money for a hedge fund, after previously working for OpenAI and the FTX Future Fund, a charitable arm of the fraudulent crypto empire of Sam Bankman-Fried, who is now in prison. Aschenbrenner ploughed that money into debt-fuelled bets on artificial intelligence companies, earning huge returns until he found out that stocks can also fall.
The trader dubbed the “Nostradamus of AI” would have been hard-pressed to foresee how quickly his high-flying hedge fund would run into trouble.
The firm’s rapid downward spiral is a familiar tale, as Silicon Valley and Wall Street once again threw their weight behind a bright-eyed but untested investor who promised this time would be different. “Everybody always wants to find the next golden child,” said one longtime hedge fund executive. “It just keeps happening.”
In less than 24 hours — which included a conversation between Griffin and Aschenbrenner — Griffin’s Citadel hedge fund reached out to Situational Awareness and snapped up the investments at a discount, according to a person familiar with the matter who asked not to be identified citing private information.
It was a startling reversal for Aschenbrenner, a former researcher at OpenAI who – before starting his hedge fund roughly two years ago — had no previous investment experience. His fledging firm has watched its assets plunge from $45bn at the start of July to about $10bn.
 Continue reading...
